Subject: Private VPC deployment — verification & canary criteria

Hi Sofia,

Thanks again for the walkthrough today. Our infra team is pulling together a short operational checklist we can use during the first two canary waves for the private VPC deployment. Before we lock it down, can you confirm Redwood's expectations for the control-plane/data-plane verification steps and the minimum canary success criteria? Specifically: 

- What control-plane health checks should we validate (etcd/k8s API responsiveness, controlplane certificate propagation windows)?
- For data-plane probes, are there token-level latency SLOs we should measure end-to-end from our edge to the inference nodes?
- Any recommended probe cadence and sample sizes for the first 24 hours?

We're assembling an evidence bundle for our security team and would like to include a short list of required logs/traces Redwood will provide during canary. I've attached our draft checklist (vpc_canary_checklist.xlsx).

Appreciate the help — goal is to minimize back-and-forth during cutover.

Best,
Alex Mercer
Head of Infrastructure, Acme Corp

Subject: Re: Private VPC deployment — verification & canary criteria

Alex — thanks for the clear ask and the checklist. Quick answers up front, then a short playbook we can use for canary windows.

Control-plane verification (minimum):
- API responsiveness: 99th percentile API latency < 200ms for control plane queries under expected load.
- Certificate propagation: new certs visible to all control-plane replicas within 60s (we'll provide certificate rotation timestamps).
- Leader election stability: no more than 1 leader transition per 30m during steady-state proving.

Data-plane probes (minimum):
- Token-level latency (edge -> inference node): p50 < 60ms, p95 < 250ms for short prompt path (<= 512 tokens).
- Error budget: < 0.5% 5xx or connection failures across sampled traffic during canary.

Probe cadence & sample sizes:
- First 2 hours: high cadence (1 probe / 15s) across 3 regions/nodes to catch flakiness.
- Next 22 hours: reduced cadence (1 probe / 5m) across full canary slice.
- Sample size: aim for >= 10k token events in the first 24h for meaningful p95/p99 estimates.

Logs/traces we will provide during canary:
- Control-plane audit logs (RBAC, API calls) with timestamps (we'll share a filtered set).
- Per-request tracing headers and sampling traces for up to 5% of requests (linkable to your probe IDs).
- Token-level latency histograms and per-model KV cache hit rates.

Attached: deployment-probe-specs.pdf with probe payloads, expected response shapes, and example curl commands.

Next steps (short):
1) You populate any missing test endpoints in your checklist and re-upload.
2) Marissa and Jonas will run an internal pre-canary test tomorrow against a staging slice and capture baseline metrics.
3) We'll schedule the canary cutover window and share a mutually-agreed rollback plan (window + monitoring escalation).

Will follow up after Marissa's run.

—Sofia
Sofia Ivanova
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: deployment-probe-specs.pdf (application/pdf)]

Subject: Re: Private VPC deployment — verification & canary criteria

Following Sofia's note — ran the short staging sweep this morning against the same model family you plan to run. High level findings attached and a short ops checklist below.

Staging summary (key items):
- Control-plane API p95 during load sweep: ~180ms (within target).
- Observed a periodic 5xx spike aligned with a single node's kernel update — resolved by draining and reprovisioning the node.
- KV cache hit rate averaged 72% on warm prefix traffic; expect canary to show variance as cache warms.

Ops checklist for the canary window (check in sequence):
1) Pre-cutover: confirm routing TTLs and BGP announcements from Acme edge are synchronized to our expected prefix list (Jonas to validate).
2) Provision a dedicated monitoring index for canary traces (so we can easily slice data in the first 6h).
3) Enable higher sampling on traces for the first 2h (5% -> 20%) then drop to 5%.
4) Pre-agree rollback thresholds: any sustained p95 token latency > 350ms for > 15m OR error rate > 1% triggers rollback.
5) Post-cutover evidence: send the first 1000 trace IDs and the control-plane audit bundle to infra-eng@acme-corp.com.

I attached the raw run log and a short CSV of the probe times. If Alex/Acme can confirm the BGP and routing TTL step, we can book the canary slot for Friday 04:00–06:00 PST (low-traffic window).

-M
Marissa Cole
Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: staging-sweep-results.csv]

Alex, Sofia — quick confirmation from routing side:

- BGP announcements verified; TTLs and prefix list matched to our expected table.
- We recommend adding a second announcement path (backup) for the canary window to reduce transient blips during upstream maintenance.

If Acme is good with the Friday 04:00–06:00 PST window and the backup announcement, Redwood will:
- Kick off the high-sample tracing at 03:45 and run the probe ramp at 04:00 exactly.
- Monitor the p95/p99 token latencies and error budget dashboard; if thresholds exceeded we'll initiate rollback and notify on the escalation channel (partners@edgecloud.io and infra-eng@acme-corp.com).
